key_insight: A self-supervised graph transformer learns spatial single‑cell interaction patterns directly from imaging‑based spatial transcriptomics, removing the need for predefined ligand–receptor lists and overcoming limited gene panels.
problem_solved: Imaging‑based spatial transcriptomics measures only limited gene panels and traditional methods rely on known ligand–receptor pairs, preventing accurate discovery of cell–cell interactions at single‑cell resolution.
method: Construct a spatial graph where nodes = cells (with measured gene features + spatial coordinates) and edges = local neighborhood relations.
Train a graph transformer with self‑supervised objectives to produce interaction‑aware cell embeddings without using ligand–receptor annotations.
Decode learned embeddings into pairwise interaction scores and spatial interaction maps, enabling discovery of interactions from incomplete gene panels.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to apply graph representation learning and self‑supervision to infer biological interactions from sparse spatial data, providing transferable models and novel benchmarks for graph attention on spatial omics.
visual_elements: Schematic tissue image overlaid with a spatial cell graph and attention weights highlighting inferred interactions
Pipeline flowchart: imaging data → spatial graph → self‑supervised graph transformer → interaction map

paper_title: Identifying spatial single-cell-level interactions with graph transformer
